Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 51, verse 7:

﴿By the winds that scatter, scattering﴾. He means: the winds that scatter the dust, scattering. It is said: the wind scattered (dharat) the dust and it scattered it (adhrat).

﴿And by those that carry a load﴾. He means: the clouds that carry the weight of water.

﴿And by those that glide with ease﴾. These are the ships that run on the water with an easy running.

﴿And by those that distribute a command﴾. These are the angels who distribute affairs among creation as they have been commanded. He swore by these things because of the indication in them of His craftsmanship and His power.

Then He mentioned what was sworn about, saying: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾ of reward and punishment, ﴿is true﴾.

﴿And indeed, the judgment [the reckoning and the recompense]﴾ [[What is between the brackets is an addition from "b".]] ﴿is to occur﴾, certainly. Then He began another oath, saying:

﴿By the sky having folds﴾. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and Ikrimah said: having good, even creation. It is said to a weaver when he weaves a garment and does it well: how fine its hubuk (ḥubuk, folds/weave)! Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: possessing adornment. Al-Hasan said: it was folded with the stars. Mujahid said: it is firm in its construction. Muqatil, al-Kalbi and al-Dahhak said: possessing pathways, like the folds of water when the wind strikes it, and the folds of sand and of curly hair; but they are not seen because of their distance from people. It is the plural of hibak and habika, and the response of the oath is His saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 51, verse 8–14:

﴿Indeed, you﴾ i.e., O people of Makkah, ﴿are in a contradictory saying﴾ concerning the Qur'an and concerning Muhammad (ﷺ). You say of the Qur'an: "Sorcery, soothsaying, and tales of the ancients," and of Muhammad (ﷺ): "A sorcerer, a poet, and a madman." It is also said: "in a contradictory saying" means: some affirming and some denying.

﴿Turned away from it is whoever is turned away﴾ is turned away from belief in it, the one who is diverted so that he denies it; that is, whoever Allah has deprived of belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in the Qur'an. It is also said that "ʿan" (from) here carries the sense of "min ajl" (because of), meaning: because of this contradictory saying, or on account of it, whoever is diverted is diverted from belief. This is because they would confront a man who wished to believe and say: "He is a sorcerer, a soothsayer, and a madman," and so they would divert him from belief. This is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid.

﴿Destroyed are the fabricators﴾ cursed are the liars. It is said: "takharrasa ʿala fulanin al-batil" (he fabricated falsehood against so-and-so). They are the ones who swore together (al-Muqtasimun), who divided among themselves the paths of Makkah, and who divided their words concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) in order to turn people away from the religion of Islam. Mujahid said: they are the soothsayers.

﴿Who are in heedlessness﴾ in unawareness, blindness, and ignorance, ﴿heedless﴾ inattentive, careless, unmindful of the matter of the Hereafter. Sahw (heedlessness) is being unaware of a thing, which is the departure of the heart from it.

﴿They ask: when is the Day of Recompense?﴾ They say: "O Muhammad, when is the Day of Judgment?" meaning the Day of Resurrection, in denial and mockery.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿The Day they are tested over the Fire﴾ i.e., this recompense will take place on a day when they ﴿are tested over the Fire﴾, that is, they will be punished and burned by it, just as gold is tested by fire. It is also said: "ʿala" here has the sense of "bi" (with), i.e., with the Fire. And the keepers of the Fire will say to them: ﴿Taste your trial﴾.

﴿Taste your trial﴾ your punishment, ﴿this is what you used to seek to hasten﴾ in the world, denying it.

ـ Translation:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them﴾ — that is, what He gave them of goodness and honour — ﴿indeed, they were before that﴾ — before their entry into Paradise — ﴿doers of good﴾ in the world.

﴿They used to sleep but little of the night﴾. Al-hujū' (sleep) is sleeping at night, not during the day. "Mā" is a superfluous particle (ṣila), and the meaning is: they used to sleep a little of the night, that is, they prayed for most of the night.

It was also said: the meaning is that the whole night in which they slept was little. This is the meaning of the statement of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, i.e.: no night passed over them without them praying during it some part of it, either from its beginning or from its middle. Anas ibn Malik said: they used to pray between Maghrib and 'Isha'. [[Narrated by Abu Dawud: 2/95; al-Tabari: 26/196; Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi in Qiyam al-Layl p. 71 (from the Mukhtasar of al-Maqrizi); and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/19; and Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir: 4/234.]] Muhammad ibn 'Ali said: they would not sleep until they had prayed 'Atamah (the night prayer). [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/196, and Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi in Qiyam al-Layl p. 25 (from the Mukhtasar of al-Maqrizi); al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 7/615 also attributes it to Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan.]] Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir said: no night came upon them which they did not spend entirely in sleep, a little of it. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/197; Muhammad ibn Nasr in Qiyam al-Layl p. 25 (from the Mukhtasar of al-Maqrizi); and Ibn Kathir: 4/234.]] Mujahid said: they did not sleep the whole night. [[Narrated by Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi in Qiyam al-Layl p. 24 (from the Mukhtasar of al-Maqrizi).]]

Some scholars stopped at His saying "qalīlan" (little), meaning: they were a little of the people, and then began: "min al-layli mā yahja'ūn" (of the night they sleep not at all). They read it as a negation, meaning: they do not sleep at all during the night, but rise for prayer and worship. This is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqatil.

﴿And at the hours before dawn they were seeking forgiveness﴾. Al-Hasan said: they did not sleep of the night except a little of it, and perhaps when they were energetic they extended (their prayer) until the pre-dawn, then they devoted themselves to seeking forgiveness at the hours before dawn. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/198; and Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi in Qiyam al-Layl p. 81 (from the Mukhtasar of al-Maqrizi).]] Al-Kalbi, Mujahid and Muqatil said: at the hours before dawn they prayed, and that is because their prayer at the hours before dawn was to seek forgiveness.

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi, who was informed by Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Mukhlidi, who was informed by Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj, who said: Qutaybah narrated to us, who said: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah descends to the lowest heaven every night when one third of the night remains, and says: 'I am the King, I am the King. Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? Who is asking Me that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I may forgive him?'" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi through the route of Qutaybah, chapter on the descent of the Lord, blessed and exalted, to the lowest heaven every night: 2/524, and he said: "a sound hadith; this hadith has been narrated through many routes from Abu Hurayrah... and these are the most authentic narrations". Also narrated by al-Bukhari in Tahajjud, chapter on supplication and prayer in the last part of the night: 3/29; Muslim in Prayer of Travellers, chapter on encouraging supplication and remembrance in the last part of the night and that it is answered, no. (758): 1/521; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/63-64.]]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who was informed by Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Na'imi, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who narrated to us from 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah, who narrated to us from Sufyan, who narrated to us from Sulayman ibn Abi Muslim, from Tawus, who heard Ibn 'Abbas say: When the Prophet (ﷺ) would rise at night for tahajjud, he would say: "O Allah, praise be to You, You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, [and praise be to You, You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, and praise be to You, You are the King of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them,] and praise be to You, You are the Truth, Your promise is true, Your meeting is true, Your word is true, Paradise is true, the Fire is true, the Prophets are true, Muhammad (ﷺ) is true, the Hour is true. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 51, verse 19:

His words, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾. The beggar (al-sa'il) is the one who asks people, and the deprived (al-mahrum) is the one who has no share in the spoils of war (al-ghana'im), and from whom nothing of the fay' (fay', property gained without battle) is given. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "The deprived is the one who has no share in Islam." Its meaning in the language is: the one who has been denied good and giving.

Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: "The deprived" is the one who abstains from asking (al-muta'affif alladhi la yas'al).

Zayd ibn Aslam said: he is the one whose fruit, crop, or the offspring of his livestock has been destroyed. This is also the saying of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: the deprived is the owner of a calamity (al-ja'ihah) [in "b" it reads: "the need"]. Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, we are laden with debt, rather we are deprived﴾ (al-Waqi'ah 56:66-67).

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 51, verses 20–23:**

﴿And on the earth are signs﴾ meaning lessons, ﴿for those who have certainty﴾, when they travel through it: the mountains, the seas, the trees, the fruits, and the various kinds of plants.

﴿And in yourselves are signs﴾, since you were a drop of semen, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, until the spirit was breathed into you.

ʿAṭāʾ reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: he means the difference of tongues, forms, colours and natures.

Ibn al-Zubayr said: he means the passage of excrement and urine, [a person] eating and drinking through one opening and expelling through two passages.

﴿Will you not then see?﴾ [Muqatil said:] ﴿Will you not then see?﴾ how He created you, so that you would recognise His power to resurrect.
[Note in the edition: this phrase is omitted in manuscript "A".]

﴿And in the sky is your provision﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujahid and Muqatil said: this means the rain, which is the cause of sustenance. ﴿And what you are promised﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: of reward and punishment. Mujahid said: of good and evil. al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: what you are promised of Paradise and Hell.

Then He swore by Himself, saying:

﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth﴾, that is: what I have mentioned regarding provision is true, ﴿just as﴾. Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr, on the authority of ʿĀṣim, read "مِثْلُ" (mithlu) with a *ḍamma* on the lām, making it a substitute for "al-ḥaqq" (the truth). The others read it with a *fatḥa* (mithla), meaning "like" (kamithli). ﴿that you speak﴾, so that you say: "There is no god but Allah."

It was said: He likened the certainty of what He reported to the certainty of human speech, just as you say: "It is true, just as you are here," and "It is true, just as you are speaking." The meaning is that it is in its truthfulness and existence like that which you know by necessity. Some of the wise said: that is, just as every person speaks with his own tongue and cannot speak with the tongue of another, so every person eats his own provision that has been apportioned to him, and cannot eat the provision of another.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 51, verses 24–29:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Has the story of Abraham's honored guests reached you?﴾ We have mentioned their number in Surah Hud [[See above: 4/187.]]. ﴿Honored﴾: [it was said: He named them honored] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "A".]] because they were noble angels with Allah. Allah the Exalted has described them: "Rather, they are honored servants" [al-Anbiya: 26]. It was also said: they were called honored because they were Abraham's guests, and Abraham was the most generous of creation, and the guests of the generous are honored.

It was also said: Abraham, peace be upon him, honored them by hastening to prepare their meal and by attending to them himself with a cheerful face.

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: "[It refers to] his serving them himself."

It was reported from Ibn Abbas: they were named honored because they came without being invited. We have also related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest." [A portion of a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Riqaq, chapter "Guarding the tongue": 11/308; and Muslim in Kitab al-Iman, chapter "Encouraging the honoring of the neighbor," no. (47): 1/68; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/312.]

﴿When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Peace, [you are] a people unknown [to me]."﴾ That is: strangers whom we do not know. Ibn Abbas said: he said to himself, "These are people we do not know." It was also said: he disapproved of their affair only because they entered upon him without asking permission. Abu al-Aliyah said: he disapproved of their greeting in that time and in that land.

﴿Then he turned﴾: he turned aside and withdrew, ﴿to his family and brought a fattened calf﴾: roasted.

﴿Then he presented it to them﴾ so that they might eat, but they did not eat. ﴿He said, "Will you not eat?" So he sensed within himself a fear of them. They said, "Do not fear," and gave him good news of a knowing boy. Then his wife came forward in a ṣarrah﴾: that is, with a cry. It was said: this was not "coming forward" from one place to another; rather, it is like the saying of the speaker, "He came at me cursing," meaning he began to curse me. That is, she began to wail, as He said: "She said, 'Oh, woe to me!'" [Hud: 72]. ﴿Then she struck her face﴾. Ibn Abbas said: she slapped her face. Others said: she gathered her fingers and struck her forehead in amazement, as is the custom of women when they are surprised by something. The root of ṣakk is striking one thing with a broad object.

﴿And she said, "An old woman, barren!"﴾ Its meaning is: will an old, barren woman bear a child? Sarah had not borne a child before that.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 51, verses 38–45:**

﴿And in Musa (Moses)﴾, meaning: We also left a sign and a lesson in the sending of Musa. It was also said that it is linked to His saying: "And in the earth are signs for those who are certain" [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] ﴿when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority﴾, with a manifest proof.

﴿But he turned away﴾, meaning he turned away and withdrew from faith, ﴿with his army﴾, meaning with his host and his soldiers, whom he relied upon for strength, like the pillar on which a building is supported. Its parallel is: "Or I would take refuge in a strong support" (Hud: 80). ﴿And he said, "A sorcerer or a madman."﴾ Abu Ubaydah said: "aw" (or) here means "wa" (and).

﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea﴾, meaning We drowned them in it, ﴿and he was blameworthy﴾, meaning he committed what deserved blame, namely claiming lordship and denying the Messenger.

﴿And in 'Ad﴾, meaning: and in the destruction of 'Ad too there is a sign, ﴿when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾, which is the one in which there is no good, no blessing, and which neither fertilizes trees nor brings rain.

﴿It left nothing it came upon﴾, of their persons, their livestock, or their wealth, ﴿without making it like that which is crumbled﴾, like a thing that is destroyed and decayed. The rameem is the vegetation of the earth when it dries and is trampled. Mujahid said: "like dry straw." Qatadah said: "like the crumbled remains of trees." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "like ground-up dust." It was also said: its origin is from decayed bone.

﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a time."﴾, meaning until the time their lifespans come to an end. That is because when they hamstrung the she-camel, it was said to them: "Enjoy yourselves for three days."

﴿But they defied the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them﴾, meaning after the passing of the three days. It is death according to Ibn 'Abbas. Muqatil said: it means the punishment. The "sa'iqah" (thunderbolt) is every destroying punishment. Al-Kisa'i read "as-sa'qah" (the outcry), which is the sound that comes from the thunderbolt. ﴿While they were looking on﴾, meaning they saw it with their own eyes.

﴿And they were not able to stand up﴾, meaning they did not rise after the punishment descended upon them, nor were they able to get up. Qatadah said: "They did not rise from that fall." ﴿Nor were they among those who could help themselves﴾, meaning they could not defend themselves against Us. Qatadah said: "They had no strength by which they could protect themselves from Allah."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 51, verses 53–56:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did they enjoin it upon one another?﴾ That is: did the first of them enjoin it upon the last of them, and some of them upon others, to deny, and did they conspire together over it? The alif in *a-tawaṣaw* is for rebuke. ﴿Rather, they are a transgressing people.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: their transgression (*ṭughyān*, excessive rebellion against God's limits) led them, because of what I gave them and the abundance I lavished on them, to deny you. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, that is, disregard them. ﴿for you are not blameworthy﴾: there is no blame upon you, for you have conveyed the message and you did not fall short in what you were commanded.

The commentators said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, and this was hard on his Companions. They thought that revelation had ceased and that punishment had come near, since the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to turn away from them. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾, and their hearts were consoled.[[Narrated by Ishaq ibn Rahwayh in his Musnad from Mujahid, and al-Busiri remained silent about it and said: "Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated it with a chain whose narrators are trustworthy." Muqatil said: The meaning is: admonish the disbelievers of Makkah with the Qur'an, for the reminder benefits whoever, in Allah's knowledge, will believe from among them. Al-Kalbi said: Admonish with the Qur'an those of your people who have believed, for the reminder benefits them.

﴿I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me.﴾ Al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak and Sufyan said: this is specific to those among the two groups who obey Him. This is indicated by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas: "And I did not create the jinn and humankind — of the believers — except to worship Me." The commentators said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, and this was hard on his Companions. They thought that revelation had ceased and that punishment had come near, since the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to turn away from them. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾, and their hearts were consoled.[[Narrated by Ishaq ibn Rahwayh in his Musnad from Mujahid, and al-Busiri remained silent about it and said: "Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated it with a chain whose narrators are trustworthy." It was also narrated by al-Tabari from Qatadah. See: al-Matalib al-'Aliyah: 3/378 with the editor's note; Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/11.]]

Muqatil said: The meaning is: admonish the disbelievers of Makkah with the Qur'an, for the reminder benefits whoever, in Allah's knowledge, will believe from among them. Al-Kalbi said: Admonish with the Qur'an those of your people who have believed, for the reminder benefits them.

﴿I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me.﴾ Al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak and Sufyan said: this is specific to those among the two groups who obey Him. This is indicated by the reading of Ibn 'Abbas: "And I did not create the jinn and humankind — of the believers — except to worship Me." Then He said in another place: "And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and humankind."[al-A'raf: 79]

Some of them said: I did not create the happy ones among the jinn and humankind except for My worship, and the wretched among them except for My disobedience. This is the meaning of the statement of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: it refers to what they were made to have of wretchedness and happiness.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "except to worship Me" means: except that I would command them to worship Me and call them to My worship. This is supported by His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: "They were commanded only to worship one God."[al-Tawbah: 31]

Mujahid said: except that they would know Me. This is the best view, because if He had not created them, His existence and oneness would not be known. Its evidence is the statement of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "Allah."﴾[al-Zukhruf: 87]

It was also said: the meaning is: except that they would submit to Me and humble themselves. The meaning of worship (*'ibadah*) in the language is humbling oneself and submission. Thus every creature among the jinn and humankind is subject to Allah's decree, humbled before His will, and no one can take for himself a departure from what he was created upon.

It was also said: "except to worship Me" means: except that they would declare Me One. As for the believer, he declares Him One in hardship and ease; as for the disbeliever, he declares Him One in hardship and calamity, but not in blessing and ease. Its explanation is the statement of Mighty and Majestic He: "So when they board ships, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion."[al-'Ankabut: 65]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 51, verse 57–60:

﴿I do not want any provision from them,﴾ meaning: I do not want them to provide sustenance for any of My creation, nor to provide for themselves. ﴿Nor do I want them to feed Me.﴾ Meaning: I do not want them to feed any of My creation. He attributed the feeding to Himself because creation are the dependents (ʿiyal) of Allah, and whoever feeds the dependents of someone has fed that someone. As came in the hadith, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿I asked you for food, but you did not feed Me.﴾ [[A portion of a hadith narrated by Muslim in al-Birr wa'l-Silah wa'l-Adab, chapter on the virtue of visiting the sick, no. (2569): 4 / 1990.]] Meaning: you did not feed My servant. Then He made clear that the Provider is none other than Him, and said:

﴿Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm.﴾ Meaning: for all of His creation. ﴿The Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾: He is the Strong, the Capable, the one who is exceedingly mighty in strength and power.

﴿For those who did wrong﴾: those among the people of Makkah who disbelieved. ﴿A portion (dhanūb)﴾: a share of the punishment. ﴿Like the portion of their companions﴾: like the share of their companions who were destroyed from the people of Nuh, ʿAd and Thamud. The original meaning of "dhanūb" in the language is a large bucket full of water; then it was used for a share and portion. ﴿So let them not ask Me to hasten﴾: to hasten the punishment. Meaning: they are delayed until the Day of Resurrection.

This is indicated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve from their Day which they are promised.﴾ Meaning: the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the Day of Badr.
